sentences.text: Hypsilophodon was a small bipedal dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of England, reaching a maximum length of 2.3 meters.
It possessed a pointed head with a sharp beak for biting plants, and its jaws held up to eleven teeth in the upper jaw and sixteen in the lower.
The name Hypsilophodon translates to "Hypsilophus-tooth".
Its skull structure indicates the presence of cheeks, an advanced trait that would have aided in chewing.
Because of its size and behavior, this animal is frequently called the "deer of the Mesozoic" or simply the "Mesozoic deer".
Despite a long-held belief that it was armoured, the animal was actually unarmoured.
Its entire body was engineered for running, featuring a lightweight skeleton, long legs, and a rigid tail stabilized by ossified tendons.
The first remains were found in 1849 in the Wessex Formation near Cowleaze Chine on the south-west coast of the Isle of Wight.
Most known specimens were recovered between 1849 and 1921.
This small herbivore likely fed on low-growing vegetation, preferring high-quality plant material like young shoots and roots.
Research by Galton in 1971 showed that the first toe was incorrectly reconstructed and that claw curvature was not for climbing, proving it was a bipedal running form.
Like most dinosaurs, it continuously replaced its teeth in an alternating pattern, with an average spacing of approximately 2.3 between teeth of the same stage.
The Zahnreihen-spacing was about 2.3, indicating a relatively low distance between teeth of the same eruption stage.
The level of parental care remains undefined as no nests have been found, though related species suggest care occurred before hatching.
Although fossils did not form a single herd, bones accumulated gradually, often leading to the belief the animals moved in large groups.
In modern classification, Hypsilophodon is considered a basal ornithopod.
Huxley originally assigned the animal to the Iguanodontidae.
In 2014, Norman proposed a monophyletic group called Hypsilophodontia to replace the historically complicated name Hypsilophodontidae.
Hypsilophodon lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically in the late Barremian about 126 million years ago.
It inhabited the Cretaceous, the last period when non-avian dinosaurs walked the earth.
While traditionally considered an early ornithopod, recent research has questioned this classification.
It is debated whether H. wielandi is a distinct species of Hypsilophodon or synonymous with Camptosaurus valdensis.
There is debate regarding whether the front teeth of Hypsilophodon had a specialized function.
